answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie earnings to a slowly released escrow, audited at random. Like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of care, a new identity must first do verifiable work before its income unlocks; each walnut of revenue is held back and released in tranches only as audits pass. A single inlet for claims, one verified work history per identity, means spawning fake agents multiplies the waiting cost without multiplying the payout, so Sybil farming stops paying for itself.
